mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority or notary public / solicitor in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered agent of the foreign corporate shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds / source-of-wealth declaration for each ultimate beneficial owner

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP and sanctions screening is required under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act. Screen all UBOs and authorized signatories against the Global Affairs Canada Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, and the Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act list. Enhanced due diligence applies to foreign PEPs, their family members and close associates. Ongoing monitoring and 5-year record retention are required under SOR/2002-184.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ontario Business Central operated by the Companies and Personal Property Security Branch (CPPSPB), Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be expressed in English, French, or a bilingual combination using Latin characters. If a name originates from a non-Latin script, a transliteration into English or French must be provided and recorded in the registry. The name must include a mandatory corporate suffix such as 'Inc.', 'Corp.' or 'Ltd.', and must not be misleading or confusing with existing registered names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: An Ontario name reservation is initially valid for 90 days and may be extended once in writing before expiration. If the proposed name is rejected by the Director of the CPPSPB, the incorporator must file a written administrative appeal within 30 days of the refusal notice, attaching a revised NUANS name search report and a statement addressing the grounds of rejection. If the administrative appeal is unsuccessful, the incorporator may seek judicial review before the Ontario Divisional Court under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, RSO 1990, c J.1.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are generally permissible for an Ontario business corporation administering an employee share incentive trust, provided the registered office is a physical street address in Ontario staffed during ordinary business hours where process service and statutory records can be received. Post office boxes are not accepted. The principal place of administration of the ESOP trust must remain at the actual managerial location, and the Canada Revenue Agency requires all corporate records to be maintained at the registered office or at a specified alternative location.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ontario Business Corporations Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. B.16, ss. 4 and 6 (incorporation articles), s. 15 (registered office), s. 17 (by-laws), ss. 114-115 (first board of directors).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ontario Business Registry (OBR), Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery, Companies and Personal Property Security Branch (CPSPB)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. Shares may be issued for any adequate consideration as set by the board; no escrow or bank deposit required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The by-laws presented to this meeting are approved and adopted. (2) The subscription for 100 common shares by the sole incorporator, at a price of C$0.01 per share, is accepted, and the shares are issued fully paid and non-assessable. (3) The registered office is established at 123 Main St, Toronto, ON. (4) The following individuals are elected as directors: [Names]. (5) The officers appointed are: President, Secretary and Treasurer. (6) The officers are authorized to execute all corporate filings, open bank accounts, and complete all statutory registrations. (7) Any necessary expenses are approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) request through the OBR portal. If using a name, obtain a name reservation report. Submit a corporate name request or use a numbered name (Ontario Business Corporations Act, s. 4). Review the name compliance criteria and contraindicated marks.
required_dossiers: Corporate name proposal or numbered company election
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, select an alternative and resubmit, or file an application for consent to use a non-compliant name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and submit Form 1 (Articles of Incorporation) online through OBR, including corporate name, registered office address, number of directors, share structure, and any restrictions. Pay the prescribed filing fee by credit card or Interac online.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application contains deficiencies, the OBR issues an examination report; correct the filing within 30 days and resubmit without additional fee for the same project, subject to the registry's policy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Monitor the OBR account for the electronic Certificate of Incorporation and copy of the articles. Verify the corporate name, registered office, and director names.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains errors, apply to the registry for a correction under the Business Corporations Act, s. 6.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Initial Corporate Governance and First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene an organizational meeting or sign a written resolution. Approve by-laws, elect directors, appoint officers, authorize banking resolutions, and adopt the share subscription. Ensure minutes are recorded in the corporate records.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If documentation is incomplete, adopt a subsequent consent resolution to ratify all corporate actions taken, and document corrections in the minutes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Registered Office and Statutory Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery (for notices) and corporate head office (for records)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify the registered office address at the time of incorporation, and if changed, file a Notice of Registered Office (Form 2). Maintain statutory records including registers of directors, shareholders, and share transfers, and accounting records, at the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Failure to maintain records is a statutory offence; cure by promptly creating and updating registers and submitting late notices if any registered office change occurred.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Ontario Ministry of Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a Business Number (BN) through CRA's Business Registration Online (BRO) service, and register for GST/HST (if required), payroll, and corporate income tax accounts. For Ontario, register for the Ontario Employer Health Tax and other applicable provincial accounts if thresholds apply.
required_dossiers: Corporate legal name and certificate of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA queries the registration, contact the Business Number Service Office and provide the corporate documents. For provincial accounts, contact the Ontario Ministry of Finance for clarification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: None applicable - the administration of employee share incentive plans is a financial administrative service and does not require an Ontario industrial or commercial manufacturing license.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required - the business operates under general corporate powers and does not require a sectoral operating permit under Ontario's regulatory framework.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ontario Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks (MECP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - the activity is an administrative service with no industrial plant or regulated operation; no Environmental Compliance Approval (ECA) required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source discharge or air emissions. If the office premise discharges sewage to a municipal sewer, compliance with municipal sewer use by-laws is required; hazardous waste (e.g. electronics) must be disposed of under O. Reg. 347.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance per the Ontario Fire Code (O. Reg. 213/07) and municipal occupancy permit; compliance with the Occupational Health and Safety Act for workplace safety, including first aid and emergency preparedness.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), including Business Registration Online, My Business Account, Represent a Client, and the CRA telephone and paper registration channels. The Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) administers customs export reporting through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS). Ontario corporate registry matters are administered separately through the Ontario Business Registry and are not substitutes for federal tax registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A corporation carrying on business in Canada, resident in Canada, or required to file a Canadian corporate income tax return must obtain a nine-digit Business Number (BN) from the CRA. A non-resident corporation may apply through CRA Business Registration Online where eligible, by submitting Form RC1 or the applicable non-resident registration request, or through an authorized representative. The corporation must provide its legal name, jurisdiction and date of incorporation, registered and mailing addresses, directors, principal business activity, accounting period, authorized contact, and details of Canadian business activities. The corporation then opens the applicable CRA program accounts, including the RC corporate income tax account and, where required or elected, the RT GST/HST account, RP payroll account, and RM import-export account. GST/HST registration is mandatory when the entity is not a small supplier and its worldwide taxable supplies, including those of associated persons where applicable, exceed the statutory threshold. Registration may be voluntary before the threshold is exceeded. A provincial Ontario corporation must also maintain its Ontario registry records, but Ontario does not issue a separate general corporate income tax identification number equivalent to the CRA BN; Ontario corporate income tax is generally administered through the federal T2 return.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no U.S.-style check-the-box election for corporations. A Canadian corporation is generally a separate taxpayer subject to federal and applicable provincial corporate income tax. A non-resident corporation remains subject to Canadian tax on income earned from carrying on business in Canada, subject to treaty relief and other statutory rules. Partnerships are generally flow-through for income tax purposes, while trusts are subject to separate trust taxation rules and may have beneficiary allocation mechanisms. An employee stock ownership or employee share incentive trust is not automatically tax-exempt and must be analyzed under the Income Tax Act provisions applicable to trusts, employee benefits, share-based compensation, designated employee benefit arrangements, and any applicable employee ownership trust rules. A corporation may make specific elections under the Income Tax Act, including elections concerning tax-deferred transfers, capital property, reorganizations, and certain trust or partnership transactions, but these are not entity-classification elections. Hybrid mismatch outcomes may arise under anti-avoidance, foreign affiliate, treaty, and hybrid instrument rules; there is no general elective hybrid classification regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax/Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST). Ontario generally applies the harmonized 13% HST to taxable supplies made in Ontario. The federal GST rate is 5% in non-participating provinces and territories. Certain supplies may be zero-rated at 0% or exempt.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies, including zero-rated supplies, measured under the applicable small-supplier rules over the relevant single-quarter or consecutive-four-quarter period. The threshold generally applies to the person and associated persons where statutory association rules require aggregation. Certain public service bodies have a CAD 50,000 threshold. Registration may be voluntary below the threshold. A non-resident may be required to register where it makes taxable supplies in Canada and is carrying on business in Canada or otherwise falls within the GST/HST registration rules, subject to special rules for non-resident digital-economy suppliers and qualifying goods, services, or platforms.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Ontario do not currently impose a general real-time electronic invoice clearance mandate, universal tax-authority invoice pre-approval, or mandatory digital tax stamp for ordinary domestic business-to-business transactions. GST/HST registrants must issue invoices or receipts containing sufficient prescribed information when requested and must retain books and records for the statutory retention period. Electronic records are acceptable if they remain reliable, accessible, and reproducible. GST/HST returns and remittances are generally filed through CRA electronic services where electronic filing is required by the registrant's circumstances or elected. Export declarations for reportable commercial goods are filed electronically through CBSA CERS. Payroll, customs, and sector-specific electronic filing obligations may apply independently.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada are generally zero-rated where the statutory GST/HST export conditions are satisfied, including delivery or transfer of possession outside Canada or shipment by the supplier to a destination outside Canada, together with prescribed documentary evidence. The supplier must establish that the goods left Canada and must retain commercial, shipping, customs, and delivery records. Services may be zero-rated where supplied to a non-resident and the specific place-of-supply and zero-rating conditions are met. The service must not fall within exclusions for services relating to real property or tangible personal property situated in Canada, services performed in respect of persons or property in Canada, passenger transportation, or other statutory exclusions. Certain advisory, administrative, financial, and plan-administration services supplied to non-residents can qualify, but the analysis depends on the recipient, use, performance, place of supply, and applicable exclusions. Zero-rated supplies support input tax credits, but zero-rating is not automatic merely because the customer is non-resident or payment is received from outside Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canadian Export Declaration or applicable CERS export report, where required by the Export and Import Permits Act, customs legislation, or the value and destination rules
Commercial invoice identifying the supplier, purchaser or consignee, description, quantity, value, currency, delivery terms, and destination
Bill of lading, air waybill, courier record, or equivalent transportation document
Packing list and proof of shipment or delivery outside Canada
Customs release, import entry, or destination-country customs record where reasonably available
Sales contract, purchase order, customer correspondence, and evidence that the recipient is non-resident where relevant to a zero-rated service
Evidence of payment and accounting records linking the export transaction to the zero-rated invoice
GST/HST tax invoices and input tax credit records supporting any refund claim
Inward remittance evidence only where commercially or institutionally requested; Canada generally does not require an inward remittance certificate as a condition for GST/HST export zero-rating
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada has no general statutory requirement to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days and no general foreign-exchange surrender rule for export receipts. CRA may deny zero-rating or input tax credits where the supplier cannot prove export, non-resident status, qualifying use, place of supply, or compliance with statutory conditions. The denied GST/HST may become payable retroactively, together with arrears interest and applicable penalties. False statements, gross negligence, knowingly false claims, or inflated refund claims may result in penalties that can reach 50% of the understated tax or improperly claimed credit or refund, in addition to interest. Failure to register, collect, remit, file, or maintain records may trigger additional administrative penalties. Deliberate fraud or tax evasion may lead to prosecution, fines, and imprisonment. Incorrect or non-compliant customs export reporting may result in CBSA Administrative Monetary Penalty System penalties, reassessment, seizure, or other customs enforcement measures. Documentation should be retained for the applicable CRA statutory period, generally at least six years from the end of the relevant tax year.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), operating under the Bank of Canada Act, in coordination with the Department of Finance Canada (policy authority), the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for bank supervision, and the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) for AML/compliance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a fully liberalized exchange-control regime; the Foreign Exchange Control Act was repealed in 1951, and no restrictions exist on current or capital account transactions. The Canadian dollar is freely convertible, with no licensing, surrender, or prior-approval requirements. Profit remittance is unrestricted subject to solvency tests under the Canada Business Corporations Act (or the Ontario Business Corporations Act) and Part XIII withholding tax on dividends, interest, or royalties payable to non-residents, as reduced by applicable tax treaties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canadian export receipts are not subject to any mandatory surrender timeline or conversion ratio. Exporters may freely retain, convert, or remit foreign currency proceeds without central bank consent. Only FINTRAC cross-border currency reporting obligations apply for physical or wire transfers exceeding CAD 10,000.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility for offshore EMIs as a primary banking relationship. Canada permits non-bank payment service providers under the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) with mandatory FINTRAC registration, but EMIs cannot accept deposits or provide direct clearing access without partnering with a prudentially regulated bank. Offshore EMIs face constraints under the Bank Act's deposit-taking monopoly and OSFI safeguarding requirements; they are not a viable substitute for domestic clearing rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In-person presence of at least one director, officer, or authorized signatory is generally required for corporate account onboarding, subject to each institution's risk-based procedure. Remote/video onboarding is available for low-risk structures, but often requires notarized or certified entity documents and a local Ontario-based representative. At minimum, a video conference with a licensed banking officer is mandatory; high-risk or complex trusts may require an in-branch interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex beneficial ownership structure (multi-layered trust or offshore shareholder)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Organizational chart, trust deed and ESOP plan documents, register of ultimate beneficiaries, professional advisor verification letters, board resolutions, and any CDD forms prescribed by the opening bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire transfers to or from high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Trade contracts, invoices, ESOP valuation reports, source-of-funds evidence, internal AML procedures, and proof of compliance with OFSI/FINTRAC sanctions screening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Low-transaction or potentially non-operational shell-like entity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan, financial statements, employee share plan trust documentation, independent legal opinion, and confirmation of substantive fiduciary activities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspected unregulated money services business (MSB) activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Legal opinion confirming the entity is not an MSB under the PCMLTFA, a declaration of the trust's dedicated ESOP administrative purpose, and evidence of regulatory exemptions where applicable.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound injections from parent entities or foreign shareholders must use SWIFT MT103 via a correspondent network to a Canadian clearing bank. Provide ISO 20022 purpose codes such as 'EQUI' for equity capital or 'INTR' for intercompany loans. All wires require the ESOP trust's legal name, account number, and proof of remitter identity. Cross-border wire reports must be filed with FINTRAC for amounts ≥ CAD 10,000. Large-value CAD settlements should be routed through Lynx (LVTS successor); settlement in foreign currency may require a nostro account at the receiving bank.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements, including employee benefit payouts or share purchase considerations, are cleared via SWIFT MT103 for cross-border wires and the Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) for domestic CAD payments. Commercial letters of credit (SWIFT MT700) may be used for documentary trade settlements, confirmed by a Schedule I Canadian bank. Each disbursement must evidence the underlying ESOP transaction and retain full audit trail for fiduciary and tax compliance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Currency options (vanilla and structured with regulated dealer)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) only for exotic non-CAD currencies under ISDA Master Agreement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ontario Annual Return (Form 1) under Corporations Information Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery (ServiceOntario), Government of Ontario
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the corporation's anniversary date (incorporation month and day)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file for two consecutive years triggers default status and administrative dissolution; impairs ability to obtain certificates of compliance or clearances.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (Federal and Ontario combined)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the corporation's fiscal period end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD $100 or 5% of unpaid tax (whichever is greater), plus 1% per month on balance up to 12 months; interest accrues on unpaid amounts; repeated failure may lead to criminal sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ontario Employer Health Tax (EHT) Reconciliation Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ontario Ministry of Finance (if provincially administered)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end, applicable only if Ontario payroll exceeds CAD $1 million in a calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest and penalties on late instalments; failure to file can lead to assessment and collection action by the Ontario Ministry of Finance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership (Individuals with Significant Control - ISC) Register Annual Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No external filing - on-site register maintained; confirmation embedded in Ontario Annual Return (Form 1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation due with Form 1; any ISC changes must be recorded within 15 days of the relevant transaction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: OBCA offences: corporation and directors/officers may face fines up to CAD $50,000 and CAD $10,000 respectively; directors may be subject to disqualification for persistent non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit threshold for private Ontario corporations; audit is required when the corporation is a reporting issuer (publicly traded) or if shareholders do not unanimously waive the appointment of an auditor under OBCA. For non-distributing corporations, all shareholders may consent in writing to dispense with an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (International Financial Reporting Standards) for publicly accountable/reporting issuers; ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) under Canadian GAAP for private corporations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under OBCA, the Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) must be updated within 15 days of any share transfer or event that changes significant control (ownership, control, or direction over 25% of shares). The Ontario Annual Return requires a declaration confirming the ISC register is accurate, accessible, and current as of the filing date.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (ISC)
Register of Share Transfers and Security Interests

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: General deductions; no specific tax holidays for ESOP administration. Potential small business deduction if CCPC, but not assumed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return; filed via CRA's e-file or NETFILE

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total revenue (gross receipts from all sources)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Canadian-source revenue if non-resident carrying on business in Canada.
Claim only expenses reasonably allocable to Canadian business operations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (revenue minus expenses and adjustments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Canadian tax rules; non-residents may be subject to Part XIV tax on certain income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal tax payable (15% of taxable income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute federal tax on Canadian-source taxable income; treaty may reduce rate.
Ontario tax applies to income attributable to permanent establishment in Ontario.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 5% of balance owing plus 1% per month up to 12 months; interest on late payments.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit Form NR-102 (for dividends) or NR-603 (for interest/royalties) to CRA, along with a Certificate of Residency (TRC) from the foreign tax authority to claim reduced rate under applicable tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory 25% for both; treaty rates vary (e.g., US: 0% interest, 10% royalties; UK: 0% interest, 10% royalties).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1 million for goods, CAD 500,000 for services, CAD 250,000 for other transactions; Local File required if total revenue > CAD 50 million or transactions exceed thresholds; Master File if total revenue > CAD 500 million and cross-border transactions > CAD 5 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have specific ESR, but GAAR and substance requirements apply to treaty benefits; corporations must have real economic activity to avoid anti-avoidance rules.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of income, false statements, or misrepresentation in tax returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fine up to 200% of tax evaded, imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable for unpaid corporate taxes and penalties; civil restitution and potential criminal charges.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating without economic substance, no real business activity, used for tax evasion or money laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA can reassess, impose penalties, and deny treaty benefits; potential criminal liability under Income Tax Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for penalties and interest if they knowingly participate.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to comply with Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) reporting requirements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to CAD 2 million for individuals, imprisonment for individuals.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally liable for fines if they knowingly participate.
